newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs rise on steady rate hopes.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs rise on steady rate hopes.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures rose on Wednesday on renewed confidence Japan would maintain a low interest rate regime against a backdrop of steady U.S. interest rates.

Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments in the first half of semi-annual congressional testimony, suggesting the Fed would not need to hike rates in the near term, cheered the market, dealers said.
September JGBs settled at a day high of 125.55 against a previous close at 125.19. The lead March Euroyen contract was at 99.06 at 1115 GMT, one tick below its day high, against a previous 99.04.
"JGBs were lifted by the U.S. bond market. It looks like U.S. interest rates won't go up based on what Greenspan said," a trader at a Japanese brokerage said.
He said the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s generous money market operations also boosted the market.
A local bank dealer said U.S. bond markets were in fact beginning to price in a U.S. rate cut in the face of continued growth without any sign of inflation.
He said the Fed might move to lower short-term rates after raising them by 25 basis points earlier this year in a pre-emptive move against inflation.
But he added that the Eurodollar futures market expected U.S. rates to remain steady.
December Eurodollars ended at 94.125 against an IMM close at 94.115 on hectic volume of 11,613 lots. March were at 94.090 against 94.085 on 12,303 lots.
